problem: Bisognano-Wichmann (A9) for Tanimoto's Borchers triple of the Bullough-Dodd S-matrix

nodes.S: Tanimoto's (M_T, U, Omega) is a Borchers triple for S_{1/2}: M_T is generated by the fields chi(xi), chi'(eta), Omega is cyclic and separating, U(x) M_T U(x)* is in M_T for x in the right wedge, and Haag-Ruelle scattering theory is available
nodes.G: Bisognano-Wichmann holds on all of H: Delta_{M_T}^{it} = U(0, -2 pi t) and J_{M_T} = J, hence wedge duality M_T' = J M_T J
nodes.F1: Compute the modular data of (M_T, Omega) on the vacuum, one- and two-particle spaces: Delta^{it} = U(0, -2 pi t) and J_{M_T} = J on H_0 + H_1 + H_2
nodes.F2: Build n-particle vectors as products of the fields chi(xi), chi'(eta) applied to Omega and prove the Tomita relation inductively in the particle number k
nodes.F3: Apply the Buchholz-Lechner / Alazzawi-Lechner Bisognano-Wichmann theorem for wedge-local fields
nodes.F4: Apply Mund's theorem that Bisognano-Wichmann follows from the particle structure of a local net
nodes.F5: Prove the Haag-Ruelle out-states at level n are sqrt(n!) P_n(slowest x ... x fastest) for all n, identifying the scattering states
nodes.F6: Verify the formal Tomita identity S_M = S_0 numerically at particle degrees 4 and 5
nodes.B1: V(t) = U(0, -2 pi t) Delta_{M_T}^{-it} and I = J_{M_T} J act as the identity on every vector of H
nodes.B2: The standard subspace of M_T is contained in the free standard subspace H_0, equivalently {S_M = S_0} is dense
nodes.B3: Bisognano-Wichmann holds on the closed span of all scattering states and that span is all of H
nodes.B4: Modular nuclearity of the map M_T(x) -> Delta^{1/4} M Omega holds for all wedge translations x
nodes.F7: So U(0, -2 pi t) Delta_{M_T}^{-it} and J_{M_T} J both act as the identity on the one-particle space H_1
nodes.F8: Created two-particle ZF vectors are never in the domain of chi'_2 because of the kinematic pole of S at i pi/3, so no product of three fields has Omega in its domain
nodes.F9: Check the hypotheses: those theorems need energy or particle-number bounds on the fields
nodes.F10: Check the hypotheses: Mund's theorem needs a local net on double cones
nodes.F11: The Moller operators are unitary onto H, so the wedge-local net is asymptotically complete
nodes.F12: The numerical agreement holds to round-off at degrees 4 and 5
nodes.B5: Any unitary W that fixes Omega, commutes with translations, maps M_T into itself and is the identity on H_1 fixes every Haag-Ruelle in and out state
nodes.B6: By Borchers' theorem Delta_{M_T}^{it} and J_{M_T} have the right commutation relations with translations, so V(t) and I commute with translations and preserve M_T
nodes.B7: Show every vector of the form A Omega with A in M_T lies in the free domain Dom Delta_0^{1/2}
nodes.B8: Establish the split property for wedge inclusions M_T(x) in M_T at large distances
